dataset_note: Facts copied from official Montana Tech pages, checked on 2026-10-17. A null field means the data was not found in the source.

credit_system.credit_hour: Credits for each course are given in semester-hours. Example from the catalog: a course shown as 4 Cr. (Hrs.: 3 Lec. 3 Lab) is a 4 semester-credit course which requires 3 weekly contact hours of lecture and 3 weekly contact hours of laboratory.
credit_system.grading: A - Excellent; B - Good; C - Average; D - Poor; F - Fail; I - Incomplete; W - Withdrawal; N - Continuing; P - Pass. GPA values (Montana University System): A = 4.0, A- = 3.7, B+ = 3.3, B = 3.0, B- = 2.7, C+ = 2.3, C = 2.0, C- = 1.7, D+ = 1.3, D = 1.0, D- = 0.7, F = 0.0.
credit_system.math_placement: All first-time students are placed in appropriate mathematics and writing courses based on their ACT/SAT scores or other placement exams.

majors.name: Computer Science, B.S.
majors.college: Lance College of Mines and Engineering
majors.description: Prepare for cutting-edge computing careers by gaining practical experience designing, building, testing, and maintaining software systems through the ABET-accredited bachelor's degree in computer science at Montana Tech. The program maintains a balance of theory and practical experience, made possible by low class sizes and a low student to faculty ratio. Required math: M 171 Calculus I, M 172 Calculus II, CSCI 246 Discrete Structures, M 333 Matrices & Linear Algebra and STAT 332 Statistics for Scientists and Engineers, plus a Data Science/Computational Math elective.
majors.career_outcomes: Graduates of the Montana Tech computer science degree program hold a variety of positions, including computer programmer, database administrator, and computer systems analyst; they also hold advanced degrees in computer science and related fields. Students have interned at companies and organizations including Google, Dish Networks, Micron Technologies, and the City of Butte.
majors.first_thing_to_check: Take CSCI 135 - Fundamentals Of Computer Science I in your first fall semester to see if programming fits you.

majors.name: Business and Information Technology, Management of Information Option, B.S.
majors.college: College of Letters, Sciences and Professional Studies
majors.description: As a BIT major with the IT option, you will learn how to analyze a variety of data in support of decision making to create value for a company using the latest technologies. The department's mission integrates a traditional business curriculum with state-of-the-art information technology. Required math: M 141 Math for Business and Social Sciences I or M 151 Precalculus, plus one statistics course (STAT 216, STAT 131 or STAT 332).
majors.career_outcomes: Many graduates work directly for IT companies, but graduates can work in nearly any company, with job opportunities in industries including entertainment, national defense, petroleum, transportation, education, health care and finance. The degree also meets the prerequisite courses for admission into an MBA program.
majors.first_thing_to_check: Take BGEN 105 - Introduction To Business in your first fall semester, then BMIS 211 - Data Analytics I in sophomore fall to test your interest in the IT side.

majors.name: Petroleum Engineering, B.S.
majors.college: Lance College of Mines and Engineering
majors.description: Petroleum engineers are concerned with the design and construction of wells and well systems for producing oil, gas, and other natural resources from the earth, and for conveying fluids into, out of, or through the earth's subsurface. The curriculum gives each student a working knowledge of the three sub-disciplines: Drilling, Production, and Reservoir Engineering. Required math: M 171 Calculus I, M 172 Calculus II, M 273 Multivariable Calculus, M 274 Introduction to Differential Equation, and STAT 332 or M 333.
majors.career_outcomes: The program page says graduates work in the petroleum industry (reservoir, production and drilling engineering) and also in geothermal, groundwater, environmental and government roles.
majors.first_thing_to_check: Take PET 201 - Elements of Petroleum Engineering in your first spring semester to see if the field fits you.

majors.name: Mining Engineering, B.S.
majors.college: Lance College of Mines and Engineering
majors.description: Design, construct, and manage surface and underground mines around the world with a degree in Mining Engineering from Montana Tech. A degree in mining engineering begins with learning the mechanics of geological materials, blasting, materials handling, mine valuation, ventilation, and designing/operating of surface and underground mines; students have access to the only on-campus underground mine in the country. Required math: M 171 Calculus I, M 172 Calculus II, M 273 Multivariable Calculus and M 274 Introduction to Differential Equation.
majors.career_outcomes: Mining engineering graduates pursue careers in coal mining, hard rock mining, open pit and underground construction management, and industrial materials and aggregate. The department reports a 96% placement rate for student interns.
majors.first_thing_to_check: Take MIN 105 - Introduction To Mining in your first spring semester and visit the Underground Mine Education Center.

majors.name: Metallurgical & Materials Engineering, B.S.
majors.college: Lance College of Mines and Engineering
majors.description: Learn how to process ores, separate valuable minerals into concentrates, produce and purify metals, manufacture metals into products, create materials, and join materials together. At Montana Tech, Metallurgical and Materials Engineering is a hybrid Bachelor of Science program that encompasses and integrates all essential aspects of materials science and process engineering. Required math: M 171 Calculus I, M 172 Calculus II, M 273 Multivariable Calculus, M 274 Introduction to Differential Equation and STAT 332 Statistics for Scientists and Engineers.
majors.career_outcomes: Job opportunities are available in industries where minerals, metals and materials are produced and consumed, including mining, manufacturing, petroleum, iron/steel making, automotive, recycling, chemicals, paper/pulp, aerospace, maintenance, corrosion and forensics. Most undergraduate students obtain summer internships or six-month co-ops.
majors.first_thing_to_check: Take EMAT 230 - Materials & The Human Experience in your first spring semester to see if materials engineering fits you.
